name: Lu Yün
bio: Lu Yün lived in the fourth century AD. Waley gives one short poem of his, “The Valley Wind,” in which a recluse stuffs his window with ferns and lets his cottage become a universe.
The poems here are Arthur Waley’s version in A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918), given with the poet’s name as spelled in those books.

poems.title: The Valley Wind
poems.author: Lu Yün
poems.collection: A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918)
poems.text:
Living in retirement beyond the World,
Silently enjoying isolation,
I pull the rope of my door tighter
And stuff my window with roots and ferns.
My spirit is tuned to the Spring-season:
At the fall of the year there is autumn in my heart.
Thus imitating cosmic changes
My cottage becomes a Universe.
